schema.label: Induction cycle 1
schema.text: All patients start with topotecan and cyclophosphamide. Three callbacks follow: treatment-arm randomization, end of induction, and end of extended induction.

schema.label: ALK branch
schema.text: A qualifying somatic ALK aberration found by APEC14B1 before induction cycle 1, day 24, removes the patient from ANBL2131 so the patient can enroll on ANBL1531 Arm E when that arm is open and the patient is eligible (section 4.1 limits this path to patients at least 1 year old). If Arm E is unavailable or the patient is not eligible, the patient stays on ANBL2131 and is randomized. An ALK result that is still unknown on day 24 does not delay randomization, and the assigned arm continues even if an ALK aberration is found later. An ALK inhibitor cannot be added on study.

schema.label: Randomization
schema.text: Randomization is after induction cycle 1, once ALK status is known or day 24 has passed. It is stratified by INRG stage (M or MS vs L2), ALK status (aberrant vs wild type vs unknown or pending), and MYCN status (amplified vs non-amplified vs unknown or pending), using APEC14B1 results. Surgery is planned after induction cycle 4 and may be after cycle 5. Dinutuximab given during induction or extended induction is investigational supply. Post-consolidation dinutuximab is commercial supply.

arms.label: Arm A
arms.text: Induction cycle 2 is topotecan and cyclophosphamide, followed by stem-cell harvest. Cycle 3 is cisplatin and etoposide. Cycle 4 is vincristine, doxorubicin, and cyclophosphamide, then surgery. Cycle 5 is cisplatin and etoposide. After the end-of-induction evaluation and callback, a good end-of-induction response goes to COG standard consolidation with tandem stem-cell transplant and radiotherapy, then post-consolidation GM-CSF, dinutuximab, and isotretinoin for cycles 1-5 and isotretinoin alone for cycle 6. Progressive disease during induction cycles 3-5, or a poor end-of-induction response, goes to extended induction or off-protocol therapy at the treating team's discretion, after disease evaluation and the callback.

arms.label: Arm B
arms.text: Same induction backbone, surgery, response branches, consolidation, and post-consolidation as Arm A, with dinutuximab and GM-CSF added on induction cycles 2-5. The schema recommends GM-CSF in cycle 2 together with G-CSF for apheresis. The treatment plan gives dinutuximab on days 2-5 of cycles 2-5, and sargramostim during cycles 3-5, strongly encouraged in cycle 2.

schema.label: Extended induction
schema.text: Irinotecan and temozolomide on days 1-5, dinutuximab on days 2-5, and GM-CSF, given as 2-cycle blocks with disease evaluation after each block. Poor end-of-induction response can continue to a maximum of 6 cycles. Progression during extended induction is off-protocol therapy. A good response proceeds to standard consolidation and the same post-consolidation immunotherapy. An end-of-extended-induction callback is required. For BSA at least 0.6 m2, temozolomide is 100 mg/m2 per dose. These patients are not eligible for primary-site CTV dose reduction.

schema.label: Primary-site radiotherapy
schema.text: Adjuvant radiotherapy to the primary site is required. The standard dose is 21.6 Gy in 12 fractions of 1.8 Gy (GyRBE where applicable). Patients with a good end-of-induction response and a primary-site complete response may receive 18 Gy to the CTV or PTV while the GTV still receives 21.6 Gy. Extended induction excludes that CTV reduction even after a primary-site complete response.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Event-free survival, comparing early chemoimmunotherapy during induction with induction that does not include it.

eligibility: Patients must enroll on APEC14B1 and consent to eligibility screening and the Molecular Characterization Initiative before ANBL2131.
Age is 30 years or younger at the initial high-risk diagnosis, and body surface area is at least 0.25 m2.
Diagnosis is neuroblastoma or nodular ganglioneuroblastoma, verified by tumor pathology or by clumps of tumor cells in the bone marrow with elevated urinary catecholamines.

High-risk disease is any age with INRG stage L2, MS, or M and MYCN amplification; age at least 547 days with INRG stage M regardless of biology; any age with initial INRG stage L1 MYCN-amplified disease that progresses to stage M without systemic chemotherapy within 6 months of diagnosis; or age at least 547 days with initial INRG stage L1, L2, or MS disease that progresses to stage M without systemic chemotherapy within 6 months.
Patients aged 365 to 546 days with INRG stage M and MYCN-non-amplified disease are excluded, as are patients at least 547 days old with INRG stage L2 and MYCN-non-amplified disease.

No prior anticancer therapy is allowed except emergency topotecan and cyclophosphamide within the permitted timing, one cycle of low- or intermediate-risk chemotherapy for disease later found to be high risk, or localized emergency radiation to a life-threatening or function-threatening site.

Known HIV infection is allowed on effective antiretroviral therapy with an undetectable viral load within 6 months, and there must be no known contraindication to peripheral-blood stem-cell collection.

Eligibility laboratories are within 7 days before enrollment: total bilirubin at most 1.5 x ULN for age, ALT at most 10 x ULN with the study ULN set at 45 U/L, and either shortening fraction at least 27% or ejection fraction at least 50%.
Renal eligibility is the age- and sex-specific maximum serum creatinine, or a 24-hour creatinine clearance or directly measured GFR of at least 70 mL/min/1.73 m2; estimated GFR is not acceptable.

Creatinine maxima in mg/dL are 0.4 under 6 months, 0.5 from 6 months to under 1 year, 0.6 from 1 to under 2 years, 0.8 from 2 to under 6 years, 1 from 6 to under 10 years, and 1.2 from 10 to under 13 years for both sexes; from 13 to under 16 years they are 1.5 for males and 1.4 for females, and at 16 years or older they are 1.7 for males and 1.4 for females.

Bone marrow failure syndromes, chronic immunosuppression other than allergy prevention or treatment and adrenal replacement, and primary immunodeficiency requiring ongoing immune globulin are exclusions; topical and inhaled corticosteroids are allowed.

Pregnancy, planned breastfeeding, and sexual activity without agreement to use effective contraception are exclusions, and a pregnancy test is required before enrollment for female patients of childbearing potential.

Staging imaging and marrow studies are obtained within 14 days before enrollment, except baseline MIBG or PET, which may be done within 14 days after cycle 1 starts without affecting eligibility; after one cycle of intermediate-risk therapy, those studies must be within 21 days before ANBL2131 therapy.

No untreated CNS disease (adequately treated CNS disease without progression is allowed).
No prior allogeneic SCT, MDS, or other malignancy.
No pharmacologic systemic steroids within 7 days or expected need on study; no other immunosuppressants.
No permanent discontinuation of anti-GD2 therapy or GM-CSF for toxicity, no prior iberdomide, and no serious allergy to thalidomide, lenalidomide, or pomalidomide.
No enzyme-inducing anticonvulsants within 7 days or strong CYP3A4 inducers/inhibitors within 14 days.
No prior unprovoked thrombosis; provoked events allowed if off anticoagulation or on a stable dose ≥ 6 weeks.
No peripheral neuropathy ≥ grade 2, no inability to take enteral medication, and not pregnant or breastfeeding; two contraception methods required with iberdomide.

eligibility: Age <= 50 years at enrollment. No lower age bound is printed.
Newly diagnosed soft tissue rhabdomyosarcoma of any subtype except adult-type pleomorphic, based on institutional histopathologic classification. FOXO1 fusion status must be known before enrollment.
FOXO1 fusion-negative: stage 2 or 3, Group III; or stage 4, Group IV, and < 10 years old. FOXO1 fusion-positive: stages 1-3, Groups I-III.
The protocol includes as embryonal RMS the 2020 WHO embryonal RMS variants (typical, dense, and botryoid) and spindle cell/sclerosing RMS. Alveolar RMS includes classic and solid variants.

FOXO1 status may be confirmed by cytogenetics, FISH, or next-generation sequencing and must be available to enroll and uploaded for randomization. Institutional PAX3 versus PAX7 testing is not required. Patients < 10 years old with stage 4 disease who are institutional fusion-negative but later fusion-positive by MCI or other testing are considered metastatic fusion-positive and come off study.
Appropriate lymph node sampling based on the primary site is required.
Lansky >= 50 if <= 16 years, or Karnofsky >= 50 if > 16 years.

Enroll before treatment begins. Protocol therapy is projected to start no later than 5 calendar days after enrollment. Eligibility labs within 7 days. Repeat CBC with differential, bilirubin, ALT, and serum creatinine before therapy if more than 7 days have elapsed. Clinical studies and disease or staging imaging, if applicable, within 21 days.
ANC >= 750/µL and platelets >= 75,000/µL.

Pediatric renal function (age < 18 years): serum creatinine at or below the age and sex maximum (male/female, mg/dL): 1 month to < 6 months 0.4/0.4, 6 months to < 1 year 0.5/0.5, 1 to < 2 years 0.6/0.6, 2 to < 6 years 0.8/0.8, 6 to < 10 years 1/1, 10 to < 13 years 1.2/1.2, 13 to < 16 years 1.5/1.4, >= 16 years 1.7/1.4; or 24-hour creatinine clearance >= 50 mL/min/1.73 m2; or measured GFR >= 70 mL/min/1.73 m2. Estimated GFR is not acceptable. Elevated creatinine from obstructive hydronephrosis secondary to tumor is still eligible if unimpeded flow is established by diversion (percutaneous nephrostomies or ureteric stents).

Adult renal function (age 18 years or older): creatinine clearance >= 50 mL/min by Cockcroft-Gault or a 24-hour urine collection, based on actual body weight capped at 140% of ideal body weight, multiplied by 0.85 if female.

Total bilirubin <= 1.5 times the upper limit of normal for age, or < 3 times the upper limit of normal for age if there is biliary obstruction by tumor. ALT <= 135 U/L. For this study the ALT upper limit of normal is set at 45 U/L.
Known HIV on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months is eligible.
No uncontrolled infection. No previous or concurrent cancer treated with chemotherapy and/or radiation. Surgical resection alone of a previous or concurrent cancer is allowed.

No CNS rhabdomyosarcoma: malignant cells in cerebrospinal fluid, intra-parenchymal brain metastases separate and distinct from the primary tumor (direct extension from a parameningeal primary is allowed), or diffuse leptomeningeal disease. No known Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease.

Chemotherapy or radiation for a non-malignant condition is allowed, but chemotherapy for the non-malignant condition must stop before protocol therapy.
